html:
The Moqoit, also called the Mocoví, are an Indigenous people of the southern Gran Chaco in Argentina, in the provinces of Santa Fe and Chaco.

They speak a Guaicuruan language related to those of the Qom and the Abipón. After the Spanish brought horses they became mounted hunters and raided Spanish towns such as Santa Fe in the 1600s and 1700s. In 1743 Jesuits founded the mission of San Javier for them, one of the reductions of the region.

In 1904 the Moqoit of San Javier rose against settlers in what is often called the last Indigenous uprising in Santa Fe; it was crushed. Today most live in Santa Fe and Chaco. Their neighbours included the Vilela.
sum: The Moqoit, also called the Mocoví, are an Indigenous people of the southern Gran Chaco in Argentina, in the provinces of Santa Fe and Chaco.
